title: Use a dot density map to show where a count clusters, each dot a stated number.
rule: Place one dot for each stated count, such as 10,000 employees, at random inside its county from a seed the chart records, and say that each dot stands for a count and marks no address. Draw the dots in the text’s ink over the land with thin gray state lines, raise the count per dot on a phone (Rule 14.12), print the count in the key at every width, and say in a note how many units draw no dot.
use_when: The reader asks where people, jobs or homes are, and a count matters more than a rate.

use_instead.when: A rate, such as a share of households
A count by state, sized as circles

text: A dot for every 10,000 shows both how many and where, so a crowded city and a thinly settled county read for what they are. Random places inside each county keep a dot from pointing at any one address.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form dot-density-map: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s83; encode id, dots and dots_phone (each county’s dots at the desk’s and the phone’s unit, from a derive script); labels.seed records the seed, labels.per the two units and labels.key the key’s words; the kit draws every dot as one path.
